findings.fix: State the eliminator and lift once, next to `toSkeleton_eq_toSkeleton_iff_nonempty_iso`: `Skeleton.ind {C} [Category C] {motive : Skeleton C → Prop} (h : ∀ X : C, motive (toSkeleton X)) (c) : motive c` and `Skeleton.lift {α : Sort*} (f : C → α) (h : ∀ X Y, Nonempty (X ≅ Y) → f X = f Y) : Skeleton C → α` with `lift_mk`; or the `ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory` variants taking `(hX : P X)` explicitly, matching the lemma already there. Keep `SimpleFDRepClasses.mk` (its `[Simple X]` instance binder does earn its place) and make `ind`/`lift`/`lift_mk` one-line specialisations of the general versions.
findings.issue: `SimpleFDRepClasses.ind` (103), `lift` (112) and `lift_mk` (121) are stated only for `Skeleton (FDRep.simpleObjects k G).FullSubcategory`, but their statements and proofs use nothing about `FDRep`, `Simple`, `k` or `G`: `ind` is `Quotient.ind`, `lift` is `Quotient.lift` plus `P.ι.mapIso`, `lift_mk` is `rfl`-by-simp. The PR already recognised this level for the companion lemma by putting `toSkeleton_eq_toSkeleton_iff_nonempty_iso` in root `CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty` (line 50). Mathlib has no `Skeleton` eliminator (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Skeletal.lean` supplies only `toSkeleton_eq_toSkeleton_iff`, line 156), so the general form is genuinely missing and any other consumer of a skeleton — e.g. the character-table work over simple objects — must re-derive it.

findings.fix: Split the variable blocks at lines 62 and 80: state `simpleObjects`, the closure instance, `SimpleFDRepClasses`, `mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`, `ind`, `lift`, `lift_mk` at `[CommRing k] [Monoid G]`, and open a second block with `[Field k]` for `toSimpleSubmoduleClasses` and its `simp` lemma.
findings.issue: `[Field k]` is visibly unused by `FDRep.simpleObjects` (65), its `IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms` instance (67), `SimpleFDRepClasses` (84), `mk` (91), `mk_eq_mk_iff` (96), `ind`, `lift` and `lift_mk`; all of these need only that `FDRep k G` is a category with zero morphisms. Only `toSimpleSubmoduleClasses` (131) and `toSimpleSubmoduleClasses_mk` (144) use fieldness, via `FDRep.isIrreducible_of_simple` and `Representation.IsIrreducible`'s `IsSimpleModule` instance. This is stronger than Mathlib's own convention in the same theory.

summary: The dictionary and the classification statements sit at the right level, but the skeleton API in FDRepClasses.lean is specialised where it is purely general: ind/lift/lift_mk use nothing about FDRep or Simple, and the [Field k] hypothesis is unused by everything up to toSimpleSubmoduleClasses.
